note: Shoot or don't shoot trainer (#/train/decide). Every rule is copied from a Hunt Mentor lesson, which carries the original source and date. c is the certainty % from that lesson, or "Tip" for opinion. s is a key in sources, p the page or section. l is the lesson id, lh the lesson screen title (matched at run time, so a renamed screen falls back to the lesson start). pic is a key in pics: a diagram (d, found inside lesson l by its aria label prefix a) or a credited photo (p). h: 1 marks the Harrison deer set (MUs 2-18, 2-19, 2-8), served first.

ph-bt-buck.author: Philip Cohen
ph-bt-buck.cap: Columbian black tailed buck in the Dungeness River, Washington, a doe at left. Red brown coat, dark tail, forked antlers like a mule deer.

ph-bt-doe.author: Walter Siegmund (talk)
ph-bt-doe.cap: Black tailed doe, Washington. The whole top of the tail is dark, not just the tip like a mule deer.

ph-bt-bedded.author: Buiobuione
ph-bt-bedded.cap: Young black tailed buck bedded by a highway, Ucluelet, Vancouver Island. Bedded deer show only head, ears and back.

ph-bt-young.author: Gordon Leggett
ph-bt-young.cap: Young black tailed buck, Victoria, BC. Note the wide tail, dark brown to black on top, held down.

ph-wt-buck.author: Famartin
ph-wt-buck.cap: White tailed deer buck, side view, New Jersey. Brown tail with white edges, antler tines rising from one main beam.

ph-md-front.author: Matt Reinbold from USA
ph-md-front.cap: Mule deer buck, front view, North Dakota badlands. Huge ears held out to the side, white throat patch, antlers that fork and fork again.

ph-md-rear.author: USFWS Mountain-Prairie
ph-md-rear.cap: Mule deer buck from behind, Colorado. Big white rump patch and a thin rope tail with a black tip.

ph-md-run.author: Wingchi Poon
ph-md-run.cap: Mule deer running away, California. From behind: white rump, thin tail with a black tip, held down even when running. Taken in California; the dark tail means it may be a black tailed deer or a cross.

ph-md-cover.author: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Headquarters
ph-md-cover.cap: Mule deer buck in brush, Malheur refuge, Oregon. In cover, look for the ears and the antler tines first.

ph-md-side.author: Marshal Hedin from San Diego
ph-md-side.cap: Mule deer buck, side view, in snow, Siskiyou County, California. Grey coat, white rump, black tipped tail, forked antlers.

ph-md-distance.author: BLM Oregon & Washington
ph-md-distance.cap: Mule deer at distance in sagebrush, eastern Oregon. Grey bodies, white rumps and big ears are what you pick out first.

ph-bb-sow.author: Neal Herbert
ph-bb-sow.cap: Black bear sow with two cubs, one black and one cinnamon, Yellowstone. Colour phases mix in one family. Cubs and sows with cubs are protected in BC (VERIFY page).

ph-griz.author: NPS/Jim Peaco
ph-griz.cap: Grizzly walking in snow, Yellowstone. The hump is the highest point of the back; the rump sits lower.

zones.a: Zones of fire, seen from above. Walking side by side: hunter
zones.alt: Zones of fire, seen from above. Walking side by side: hunters A and B walk in sight of each other and in line. Each shoots only in an arc of about 45 degrees straight ahead of them; the wedge between them is NO SHOT. Small boat: two hunters sit back to back, the bow shooter covers the arc off the bow and the stern shooter the arc off the stern; never shoot toward your partner. Sit to shoot, never swing past your partner, motor off and anchored. The width of the boat arcs is an illustration only: no source gives an angle for a boat.

formation.a: Top view of two hunters walking side by side in a line, in s
formation.alt: Top view of two hunters walking side by side in a line, in sight of each other, wearing orange. Each has a zone of fire of about 45 degrees straight ahead. The ground between them and behind them is a no shot zone.

push.a: A simple push, map view. A strip of cover narrows to a funne
push.alt: A simple push, map view. A strip of cover narrows to a funnel. The stander sits at the crossing at the funnel with a zone of fire pointing away, out of the cover, labelled shoot only out here. The pusher walks slowly through the cover toward the stander and a deer moves ahead of the pusher. A red dashed line with a cross: the stander never shoots back toward the pusher.

pt-tag.a: After a kill: the hunter who killed the animal cancels their
pt-tag.alt: After a kill: the hunter who killed the animal cancels their own species licence right away, before handling it. You can never use or lend another person licence.

pt-after4.a: Walk up together from behind and above. The shooter leads.
pt-after4.alt: Walk up together from behind and above. The shooter leads.

agree.a: Before every walk, agree three things: who covers left, who
agree.alt: Before every walk, agree three things: who covers left, who covers right, and the stop signal. After a shot, both unload and walk up together, the shooter leads.

fence1.a: Fence step 1: before the fence, unload the rifle. Bolt open,
fence1.alt: Fence step 1: before the fence, unload the rifle. Bolt open, magazine out, chamber empty. PROVE it safe.

gun-car.a: Firearm in a vehicle. Unloaded means no cartridge in the cha
gun-car.alt: Firearm in a vehicle. Unloaded means no cartridge in the chamber and none in an attached or inserted magazine. Magazine out, chamber empty, before it goes in the car or on the ATV. Vehicle left alone: firearm locked in the trunk, or out of sight with the vehicle locked.

legal-flow.a: Flowchart: is it legal to shoot? Answer nine questions in or
legal-flow.alt: Flowchart: is it legal to shoot? Answer nine questions in order. Yes goes down to the next question; no at any step goes right, to DO NOT SHOOT. 1. Licences on me? 2. Legal hours right now? 3. Season open, MU (Management Unit), sex? 4. 100% sure what it is? 5. Off road, out of vehicle? 6. Over 100 m from buildings? 7. Allowed on this land? 8. Safe backstop? 9. Clean shot, in my range? All 9 yes: you may shoot. Any doubt at any step means no.

ring100.a: A 100 metre ring, 109 yards, around an occupied house. A dee
ring100.alt: A 100 metre ring, 109 yards, around an occupied house. A deer inside the ring: no hunting and no shooting. A deer outside the ring: check the other rules. The ring counts around an occupied dwelling house, a farm or ranch building with people or domestic animals, a church, a school building or school yard, a playground and a regional district park. Owner permission does not lift it.

road-allow.a: Top view of a road with cars. A red dashed band on each side
road-allow.alt: Top view of a road with cars. A red dashed band on each side marks the road allowance: no hunting, no shooting, and no shot across the road (99%). On a road under 3 lanes it runs 15 metres (16 yards) each side of the middle; on 3 lanes or more, 15 metres from the pavement edge; or to private or cultivated land if that comes first. On listed highways only, a further 400 metre band beyond the road allowance on each side bans bullets and slugs; a shotgun with shot is OK there. Not to scale.

enclosed.a: Three ways private or leased land counts as enclosed under t
enclosed.alt: Three ways private or leased land counts as enclosed under the Trespass Act, any one is enough. Signs: no trespassing signs clearly visible at each ordinary access point, drawn as a posted NO sign at a farm gate. Fence: a lawful fence all the way round, drawn as a field ringed by fence posts. Natural edge: a natural boundary all the way round, such as a riverbank or a hedge about 1.4 metres high. Enclosed land needs the owner's permission.

closed-places.a: Places where hunting is closed or limited. No hunting: Natio
closed-places.alt: Places where hunting is closed or limited. No hunting: National Park, no hunting at all. Ecological reserve, no hunting and no firing a gun or bow. Limited, check first: National Wildlife Areas and Migratory Bird Sanctuaries, federal bird land, closed unless a federal permit or posted notices allow it, boundaries marked with blue loon signs. BC Park: only if its own page allows hunting, and only in open season. Regional district park: most ban firing; in Regions 1 and 2, no hunting or shooting within 100 metres. Recreation site: no firing within 100 metres of camps and structures. Conservation land: call the regional office first. Reserve: private land, band office permission needed. Town: the local bylaw decides.

rec-site.a: Top view of a recreation site. The developed portion reaches
rec-site.alt: Top view of a recreation site. The developed portion reaches 100 metres in every direction from a structure, day use area, camping area or trail staging area. No firing a firearm, bow or crossbow on or into it, and no game residue there. On a recreation trail the ban applies only where posted.

perm-lease.a: Four cards. Grazing lease with cattle on it: ask the lessee.
perm-lease.alt: Four cards. Grazing lease with cattle on it: ask the lessee. Grazing lease with no cattle: the Trespass Act still applies. Cultivated land, meaning crops, hay or orchards: ask the owner. Any dwelling or farm building with people or animals: no hunting or shooting within 100 metres. Land that is not fenced or posted can still need a yes.

perm-note.a: A written permission note to keep in your pocket. Lines for
perm-note.alt: A written permission note to keep in your pocket. Lines for the owner's name, phone number, date, the area you may hunt, places to avoid, and your two names.

unlawful1.a: Icon cards, top unlawful acts part 1, with the item number f
unlawful1.alt: Icon cards, top unlawful acts part 1, with the item number from the page 11 list. Item 1: cancel your species licence before you touch big game. Item 2: never use another person's licence. Item 22: no hunting from a motor vehicle. Item 28: no loaded firearm in or on a vehicle such as a truck or ATV. Items 37 and 38: hunt only in legal hours, never at night. Item 38, second: no light of any kind to hunt by.

r2-deer-bars.a: Season bars for Region 2 black tailed deer, the mule deer ro
r2-deer-bars.alt: Season bars for Region 2 black tailed deer, the mule deer rows on synopsis page 28: general, youth and senior seasons. Bucks in 2-2 to 2-4, 2-6 to 2-8, 2-13 to 2-15 and 2-17 to 2-19: 10 September to 15 December. Bucks in 2-9 to 2-11: 10 September to 30 November. Bucks in diamond 2-5 and 2-12: 10 September to 30 November, diamond means bag 1 buck. Bucks in triangle 2-16: 10 September to 15 December. Antlerless in triangle 2-16: 5 to 20 November. Antlerless, Youth/Senior Only, three stars, in 2-11 two stars, Map B20 Pemberton zone only: 10 to 30 September. Antlerless, Youth Only, one star, in triangle 2-16: 21 to 31 October.

r2-bow-bars.a: Season bars for Region 2 black tailed deer, Bow Only, synops
r2-bow-bars.alt: Season bars for Region 2 black tailed deer, Bow Only, synopsis page 28. Triangle: Bowen and Texada bag 3(2). Bucks in triangle 2-2 to 2-19: 1 to 9 September. Bucks, triangle star 2-16, Bowen Island only: 1 September to 15 December. Antlerless, triangle star 2-16, Bowen Island only: 5 November to 5 December. Either sex, triangle star 2-16, Bowen Island only: 1 to 15 January. Either sex, asterisk 2-16, Texada Island only: 16 December to 15 January.

r2-deer-bag.a: Grid: Region 2 deer bag limits. Black tailed deer a licence
r2-deer-bag.alt: Grid: Region 2 deer bag limits. Black tailed deer a licence year: 2. Of those, antlerless at most: 1. White tailed deer: 0. Bowen and Texada islands: 3(2): 3. Buck, 2-5 and 2-12, Sept 10 to Nov 30: 1. Province wide, never more deer a year: 3.

r2-no-hunt.a: Cards: Other no hunting notices. Burns Bog, 2-4: No hunting
r2-no-hunt.alt: Cards: Other no hunting notices. Burns Bog, 2-4: No hunting or trapping on the partnership lands. Herrling Island, 2-3: White tailed deer live there. No open season for them. Regional district parks: No hunting or shooting within 100 m.

r2-roads.a: Cards: No shooting along roads, hunting allowed. FVRD roads:
r2-roads.alt: Cards: No shooting along roads, hunting allowed. FVRD roads: No shooting within 400 m of select roads, unless lawfully hunting or trapping. Map B11 Squamish Valley: No Shooting Areas. Firearms for hunting permitted. Map B33 Chehalis, 2-19: No Shooting Area. Firearms for hunting permitted.

r2-b29.a: Cards: Maps B29 to B32. B29 Elbow Lake: No Shooting Area. MU
r2-b29.alt: Cards: Maps B29 to B32. B29 Elbow Lake: No Shooting Area. MU 2-19. B30 Yale: No Shooting Area. MU 2-18. B31 North Thormanby Island: No Shooting or Hunting Area. MU 2-16. B32 Hemlock Valley: No Shooting Area. MU 2-19.

r2-fvsla.a: Fraser Valley Special Area, synopsis pages 8, 27 and 29, as
r2-fvsla.alt: Fraser Valley Special Area, synopsis pages 8, 27 and 29, as icon cards. Where: all of MU 2-4, and MU 2-8 inside Maple Ridge, Pitt Meadows, Mission and Coquitlam (Map B10). You need: the Special Area licence, $10.00, plus $1,000,000 liability insurance. Format: electronic only, on your FWID (Fish and Wildlife ID) profile. Gulf Islands Special Area: Region 1 islands only, $2.00; Bowen and Texada do not need it (95%, my reading).

fv-noshoot.a: More no shooting rules near Mission. No shooting: Sumas Moun
fv-noshoot.alt: More no shooting rules near Mission. No shooting: Sumas Mountain, all of Electoral Area H of the Fraser Valley Regional District is a No Shooting Area, 98 percent. Regional District Parks in Regions 1 and 2: no hunting or shooting within 100 metres, 99 percent. Nicomen Island lowland: rifles prohibited, 90 percent. Limits: Fraser Valley Regional District roads, no discharge within 400 metres except lawful hunting or trapping, 99 percent. Highway 7 east of Mission and Highway 1 east of Chilliwack: shot only within 150 metres, 98 percent. Abbotsford bylaw: discharge limited to farmers protecting stock, slaughter and licensed ranges, 70 percent, VERIFY.

hours.a: Day timeline: legal hours run from one hour before sunrise t
hours.alt: Day timeline: legal hours run from one hour before sunrise to one hour after sunset. Outside that, no hunting. Following a trail with a rifle counts as hunting. Never use a light or headlamp with a rifle. Tracking with no rifle, just finding a dead deer, is not settled: verify with a conservation officer.

sk-fence.a: A blood trail reaches a fence with a No Trespassing sign. Th
sk-fence.alt: A blood trail reaches a fence with a No Trespassing sign. The hunter stops. 1: ask the owner first, in writing if you can. 2: no answer, call a conservation officer. The Trespass Act has no tracking exception.

track-flow.a: Flowchart of what to do after the shot, in order: 1 watch, 2
track-flow.alt: Flowchart of what to do after the shot, in order: 1 watch, 2 listen, 3 mark, 4 wait, 5 read the hit site, 6 trail, 7 grid search, 8 get help.

blood-chart.a: Blood sign chart: what the blood looks like, what was hit, a
blood-chart.alt: Blood sign chart: what the blood looks like, what was hit, and how long to wait before you follow. Pink, frothy blood with bubbles: lungs, wait 30 minutes. Bright red, lots of it: heart or a big artery, wait 30 minutes. Dark red with no bubbles: liver, wait 4 to 6 hours. Thin, green brown with food bits and a smell: gut, wait 6 to 8 hours. Thin, patchy blood while the deer keeps running: muscle or leg, wait 30 to 60 minutes. Opinion from hunter education, not law (70%).

no-shoot.a: Six small pictures of shots to pass: a deer facing straight
no-shoot.alt: Six small pictures of shots to pass: a deer facing straight at you, a deer walking straight away, a running deer, a deer skylined on a ridge with only sky behind it and no backstop, a deer behind brush, and a deer with another deer behind it. Not sure? That is a no. Hunt tomorrow.

vitals-deer.a: Deer, broadside, a male with antlers, drawn as a field guide
vitals-deer.alt: Deer, broadside, a male with antlers, drawn as a field guide plate with the shoulder blade, lungs, heart and paunch shown through the body. Aim up the back of the front leg, one third up the chest: both lungs, top of the heart. A dashed circle marks the vital zone with margin, about 20 to 25 centimetres, 8 to 10 inches. Three steps: broadside and standing, near leg forward, aim. Below, three top views: broadside is best; quartering away is good, the bullet exits the far shoulder; quartering to is for experienced hunters only, beginners wait.

vitals-bear.a: Black bear, broadside, drawn with the lungs and heart shown
vitals-bear.alt: Black bear, broadside, drawn with the lungs and heart shown through the body. A dashed line inside the outline shows the real body under the hair: hair adds 8 to 10 centimetres (70%), so the bear looks bigger than it is. The heart sits low, behind the shoulder; the lungs reach past the middle of the body. Aim halfway up, tight behind the shoulder, with the near leg forward (85%). Below, three top views: broadside is best; quartering away is good, aim farther back so the bullet crosses both lungs to the far shoulder; quartering to is for experienced hunters only: heavy shoulder bone and a dense skull, so wait for broadside.

angles.a: Animation seen from above, the hunter at the bottom and the
angles.alt: Animation seen from above, the hunter at the bottom and the bullet line running straight up through the lungs. The deer turns through four angles. Facing away: never, guts and hams are in the way. Quartering toward: wait, the near shoulder bone is in the way. Quartering away: good, aim so the bullet exits the far shoulder. Broadside: best, through both lungs, the biggest target. Lungs are orange, shoulder bones brown.

noshot-icons.a: Six picture tiles, each with a no sign: a deer skylined on a
noshot-icons.alt: Six picture tiles, each with a no sign: a deer skylined on a ridge with no backstop; a deer half hidden in bushes, not 100 percent sure what it is; a deer moving; a deer too far away; a deer behind brush; a buck lying down with the vitals hidden. Any one of these means no shot. Passing is a skill, a tip.

approach.a: A downed deer lying on its side, seen from above. The hunter
approach.alt: A downed deer lying on its side, seen from above. The hunter comes in from behind its back, the spine side, with the rifle ready, never from the legs side: a live deer can kick or jump up. Watch the chest for breathing, a tip.

notch.a: A generic BC resident species licence for mule deer, 2026 to
notch.alt: A generic BC resident species licence for mule deer, 2026 to 2027, with an FWID number, a licence number and a barcode. Strips run round the edges: month along the top (September to January), day down the right (1 to 31), region along the bottom (1 to 8, with 7A and 7B) and class down the left (buck, antlerless). Orange V notches are cut out at October, day 15, region 3 and buck. This card is a generic example: follow the instructions printed on your own licence.

evidence.a: Evidence of sex on a deer stays naturally attached. Buck: th
evidence.alt: Evidence of sex on a deer stays naturally attached. Buck: the unskinned tail and a testicle or part of the penis. Doe: the unskinned tail and part of the udder and teats. Both stay attached to the carcass or one part of it.

carry-all.a: Carry every species licence while hunting, cancelled and not
carry-all.alt: Carry every species licence while hunting, cancelled and not, all licence year, 95 percent. Three licences: deer, cancelled; moose, not used; black bear, not used. Timeline: from the kill until the meat is eaten, keep the papers. A mounted head or tanned hide: keep the licence forever. Lost one? Replace it at FrontCounter BC or Service BC for 10 dollars, and declare the harvest from the cancelled original, 95 percent.

transport-papers.a: Which paper goes with meat you move. Your own animal: your s
transport-papers.alt: Which paper goes with meat you move. Your own animal: your species licence travels with the meat. Someone else's animal: a Record of Receipt from the hunter. At the butcher: get a receipt showing the hunter's FWID, the species licence number, the species and the sex.

self-report.a: Accidental illegal harvest, in order. 1, cancel your species
self-report.alt: Accidental illegal harvest, in order. 1, cancel your species licence at once and write in ink that you intend to self report. Then one of these: 2, with phone signal, call RAPP at 1 877 952 7277 and follow the conservation officer. 3, if a phone is a short trip away, field dress the animal, leave the carcass there and go call. 4, if remote with no phone, field dress it, care for the carcass, and call as soon as you can. The test is how you deal with the mistake.

et-hunters.a: Do and do not cards for other hunters. Do: a truck at a pull
et-hunters.alt: Do and do not cards for other hunters. Do: a truck at a pullout means someone is on that ridge, so drive on. Do not: walk in on another hunter's stalk. Do: the first hunter on a meadow owns it for the morning. Do not: interfere with or obstruct a hunter, which is also law. Do: when you meet on a trail, unload and point the muzzle down. Do: offer a hand with the pack out.

bear-flow.a: What is the bear doing? Unaware of you: leave quietly the wa
bear-flow.alt: What is the bear doing? Unaware of you: leave quietly the way you came. Sees you but calm: talk softly and back away slowly. Agitated and huffing: calm voice, back away, bear spray ready. Coming steadily at you: yell, stand big, spray, be ready to fight. In every case, never run.

bear-warning.a: A bear telling you to back off: jaw popping, woofing, moanin
bear-warning.alt: A bear telling you to back off: jaw popping, woofing, moaning, stomping, a bluff charge that stops short, ears back and head low. It is stressed and defensive. Give it room.

bear-spray.a: Bear spray by distance, from Alberta bear safety guidance: 9
bear-spray.alt: Bear spray by distance, from Alberta bear safety guidance: 9 to 15 metres, a half to 1 second warning blast aimed slightly down. 6 to 9 metres, 1 to 2 second bursts aimed low in front of the head. 0 to 6 metres, bursts at the head. Keep some in reserve, then back away while watching the bear.

bear-kill1.a: Kill site step 1: talk and make noise while you field dress,
bear-kill1.alt: Kill site step 1: talk and make noise while you field dress, and keep the rifle and spray within reach. One of you watches.

bear-kill4.a: Kill site step 4: come back from upwind, stop at a distance
bear-kill4.alt: Kill site step 4: come back from upwind, stop at a distance and glass the meat. Moved, buried or a bear on it: leave and report.

bear-dead.a: Defensive bear contact position: lie on your stomach with yo
bear-dead.alt: Defensive bear contact position: lie on your stomach with your pack on, hands clasped over the back of your neck, legs spread so it is hard to flip you. Stay still until the bear leaves.

scenarios.q: 20 November, MU (Management Unit) 2-19, west of Harrison Lake. A black tailed doe steps out at 60 m (66 yd). Legal light, earth behind her, standing broadside.
ch: Shoot: the Region 2 limit allows 1 antlerless
Don't shoot: 2-19 is bucks only
Shoot, and your brother cancels his licence
scenarios.why: The 2-19 general season is bucks only, 10 September to 15 December. The limit of 2 with 1 antlerless is a ceiling, not a season. And only the shooter cancels a licence.
scenarios.rule: MUs 2-8, 2-18 and 2-19: bucks, 10 September to 15 December. No general antlerless season.

scenarios.q: 12 November, MU (Management Unit) 2-18, east of Harrison Lake, 9 a.m. A forked black tailed buck stands still, broadside at 80 m (87 yd). Licences on you, earth backstop, nobody beyond.
ch: Shoot: a buck is legal here today
Don't shoot: it needs 4 points
Don't shoot: November is bow only
scenarios.why: The 2-18 rows say Bucks, not 4 point bucks. A buck is a deer bearing visible bony antlers. Rifle season runs 10 September to 15 December. Every one of the 9 steps is yes.
scenarios.rule: Buck: a deer bearing visible bony antlers. 2-18 general season: bucks, 10 September to 15 December.

scenarios.q: MU (Management Unit) 2-18, late November. A buck bounds off with a wide brown tail flagged up white, then stops broadside at 90 m (98 yd).
ch: Shoot: any buck is legal in 2-18
Don't shoot: that looks like a white tail, and Region 2 has no white tail season
Shoot only if it has 4 points
scenarios.why: A wide brown tail that flags white is a white tail sign. Region 2 has no white tailed deer season at all. Not sure which deer it is? Not sure means no.
scenarios.rule: No white tailed deer season anywhere in Region 2. Some live near Hope at Herrling Island.
scenarios.lh: Black tailed deer or mule deer?

scenarios.q: 5 September, MU (Management Unit) 2-18. You carry your rifle to scout. A young black tailed buck walks out at 50 m (55 yd).
ch: Shoot: the buck season is open
Don't shoot: 1 to 9 September is bow only
Shoot if it is broadside
scenarios.why: From 1 to 9 September the 2-2 to 2-19 buck row is Bow Only. The rifle season opens 10 September.
scenarios.rule: Region 2 bucks, 1 to 9 September: bow only. General season from 10 September.

scenarios.q: 17 December, MU (Management Unit) 2-19. Fresh snow, and a good buck crosses the old road at 70 m (77 yd).
ch: Shoot: the rut is still on
Don't shoot: the season closed 15 December
Shoot: snow seasons run to January
scenarios.why: The 2-19 buck season ends 15 December. After that there is no open season for deer there.
scenarios.rule: 2-19 bucks: 10 September to 15 December.

scenarios.q: You took a buck in MU (Management Unit) 2-19 in October. In November you hold a second, unused mule deer species licence. A legal buck stands broadside in 2-18, all 9 steps yes.
ch: Shoot: the Region 2 limit is 2 deer a licence year
Don't shoot: the limit is 1 deer
Don't shoot: one licence per hunter per year
scenarios.why: Region 2 allows 2 mule (black tailed) deer a licence year, at most 1 antlerless. You may hold up to 3 mule deer species licences. Province wide, 3 deer at most.
scenarios.rule: Region 2 deer limit: 2 a licence year, at most 1 antlerless. Up to 3 mule deer species licences.

scenarios.q: Sunrise at your spot above Harrison is 7:20 a.m. At 6:05 a.m. you can just make out a buck at 50 m (55 yd).
ch: Shoot: you can see it
Don't shoot: legal hours start at 6:20 a.m.
Shoot: deer hours start 2 hours before sunrise
scenarios.why: Big game hours start 1 hour before sunrise. 7:20 minus 1 hour is 6:20 a.m. At 6:05 it is still closed.
scenarios.rule: No hunting game (except migratory birds) from 1 hour after sunset to 1 hour before sunrise.

scenarios.q: Sunset is 4:25 p.m. It is 5:10 p.m. on a cutblock in MU (Management Unit) 2-19, still light enough to be 100% sure: a buck, broadside, 60 m (66 yd), earth behind.
ch: Shoot: legal until 5:25 p.m.
Don't shoot: hunting ends at sunset
Don't shoot: hunting ends 30 minutes after sunset
scenarios.why: Deer hours run to 1 hour after sunset: 4:25 plus 1 hour is 5:25 p.m. The 30 minute rule is for ducks and geese. Judging sunset where you stand is your job.
scenarios.rule: Big game: legal from 1 hour before sunrise to 1 hour after sunset. Migratory birds: 30 minutes.

scenarios.q: A hill inside Mission city limits, MU (Management Unit) 2-8. You carry your hunting licence and deer species licence only. A legal buck in season walks out.
ch: Shoot: those two licences cover 2-8
Don't shoot: inside Mission limits you also need the Fraser Valley Special Area licence and $1,000,000 liability insurance
Shoot with a shotgun only
scenarios.why: Map B10: anyone hunting in MU 2-4, or in 2-8 inside Mission, Maple Ridge, Pitt Meadows or Coquitlam, needs the Special Area licence plus $1,000,000 public liability insurance. Mission bylaw areas add more limits.
scenarios.rule: Fraser Valley Special Area licence ($10) and $1,000,000 liability insurance inside Mission city limits.
scenarios.lh: The extra licence you need in Mission

scenarios.q: A buck feeds in a field on the Harrison Mills and Nicomen lowland, off Highway 7. No sign in sight. You hold your rifle.
ch: Shoot: no sign means open
Don't shoot: that lowland bans rifles
Shoot if it is over 100 m from the house
scenarios.why: The Closed Areas Regulation bans rifles on the Harrison Mills and Nicomen lowland, and allows only shot on much of it. Hunt deer up in the hills, not on the flats. A missing sign is no defence.
scenarios.rule: Harrison Mills and Nicomen lowland: no rifles, shot only on much of it. 99% for the schedules, 85% for the app's reading of the boundary.
scenarios.lh: Logging roads and the closures here (2 of 2)

scenarios.q: A buck stands 120 m (131 yd) from Highway 7, east of Mission. Rifle in hand, off the road, earth behind it.
ch: Shoot: you are well past the 15 m road allowance
Don't shoot: within 150 m of Highway 7 only shot is allowed
Shoot from the shoulder for a better rest
scenarios.why: Highway 7, east of Mission to Highway 1, is shot only within 150 m. A rifle bullet is not shot. The road allowance rule comes on top of that.
scenarios.rule: Highway 7 and Highway 1 here: firearms using shot only within 150 m.

scenarios.q: Crown land 200 m (219 yd) off the Weaver Lake FSR (Forest Service Road), inside its 400 m band. A legal buck, in season, earth backstop, no house or sign nearby.
ch: Shoot: lawful hunting is allowed in the band
Don't shoot: nobody may fire within 400 m
Shoot only with a shotgun
scenarios.why: The 400 m bands on the Francis Lake, Weaver Lake and Sts'ailes (West) FSRs ban discharge unless you are lawfully hunting or trapping. Hunting is allowed. Target shooting is not.
scenarios.rule: No discharge within 400 m of these roads unless lawfully hunting or trapping. 99% for the rule, 90% for the app's reading that hunting is allowed.
scenarios.lh: Logging roads and the closures here (2 of 2)

scenarios.q: MU (Management Unit) 2-19. A buck stands 300 m (328 yd) off the Chehalis road, about 1 km north of Elbow Lake.
ch: Shoot: hunting is allowed along the Chehalis roads
Don't shoot: this is the Map B29 Elbow Lake No Shooting Area
Shoot if it is broadside
scenarios.why: Map B29: a No Shooting Area 800 m either side of the Chehalis road for 2.4 km north of Elbow Lake. 300 m off the road is inside it. The Map B33 bands that allow hunting are a different area.
scenarios.rule: Map B29 Elbow Lake: No Shooting Area, 800 m either side of the Chehalis road for 2.4 km north of Elbow Lake.
scenarios.lh: Logging roads and the closures here (2 of 2)

scenarios.q: Driving up toward Hemlock Valley in MU (Management Unit) 2-19, you park and walk. A buck stands 40 m (44 yd) from the Hemlock Valley road.
ch: Shoot: you are off the road and out of the truck
Don't shoot: the Hemlock Valley road is a No Shooting Area band
Shoot with a rest on the truck
scenarios.why: Map B32 Hemlock Valley: a No Shooting Area 50 m, then 150 m, either side of the Hemlock Valley road. 40 m is inside both widths.
scenarios.rule: Map B32 Hemlock Valley: No Shooting Area 50 m, then 150 m, either side of the road.
scenarios.lh: Maps B29 to B32: Elbow Lake, Yale, Thormanby, Hemlock Valley

scenarios.q: MU (Management Unit) 2-19, within 400 m of the Chehalis River high water mark, inside the Map B33 bands. A legal buck in season, safe backstop.
ch: Shoot: firing to hunt is allowed in the B33 bands
Don't shoot: the bands are No Shooting for everyone
Only a bow is allowed there
scenarios.why: Map B33 Chehalis Fleetwood: discharge of firearms for the purpose of hunting is permitted. No target shooting there.
scenarios.rule: Map B33 Chehalis Fleetwood No Shooting Area: firing for hunting permitted (MU 2-19).
scenarios.lh: Map B33 Chehalis and the 2-19 road areas

scenarios.q: Following a ridge near Harrison, your map shows you just crossed into Sasquatch Provincial Park. A buck stands below you.
ch: Shoot: provincial parks are open to hunting
Don't shoot: confirm on the park's own page first; the app has not checked this park
Shoot if no sign says closed
scenarios.why: Many BC Parks ban hunting and firing a firearm. The rule puts the check on you: confirm on the park's own BC Parks page that hunting is allowed. Sasquatch Park's status is VERIFY in the app, so treat it as closed.
scenarios.rule: Before you hunt a BC Park, confirm on its BC Parks page that hunting is allowed. Sasquatch and Kilby parks: VERIFY.

scenarios.q: Farm edge near Agassiz, MU (Management Unit) 2-18. The farmer gave you written permission. A buck stands 80 m (87 yd) from the barn, which has cattle in it.
ch: Shoot: you have written permission
Don't shoot: inside 100 m of an occupied farm building
Shoot if the barn is behind you
scenarios.why: No hunting or shooting within 100 m of a dwelling, or a farm or ranch building with people or domestic animals in it. Permission does not lift it.
scenarios.rule: No hunting or shooting within 100 m (109 yd) of a house, school, church, playground, regional district park, or an occupied farm building.

scenarios.q: A buck walks off the cutblock onto private land. A No Trespassing sign hangs at the gate. You have no permission.
ch: Shoot: the buck was on Crown land a minute ago
Don't shoot: posted private land is closed without the owner's permission
Shoot, then ask the owner
scenarios.why: Signs at each ordinary access point make private land enclosed under the Trespass Act. A legal buck shot while trespassing is an illegal buck.
scenarios.rule: Enclosed land (signs, a lawful fence or a natural boundary) is closed without permission. Killing wildlife while breaking another law is unlawful.
scenarios.lh: The Trespass Act in plain words

scenarios.q: You and your brother walk a cutblock edge side by side, in sight. A buck jumps up and runs into the gap between you.
ch: Swing with it and shoot
Hold fire: the gap is a no shot zone
Shoot only if it stops
scenarios.why: Each hunter shoots only in about 45 degrees straight ahead. The middle and behind are no shot zones. Never swing the muzzle out of your slice, even for a running deer.
scenarios.rule: Zone of fire: about 45 degrees straight ahead for each hunter. The wedge between you is no shot.

scenarios.q: Your brother walks an alder strip toward you while you sit the crossing. A buck breaks back toward the cover he is walking in.
ch: Shoot: it is in range
Don't shoot: the stander shoots only away from the pusher's line
Shoot over his head
scenarios.why: On a push the stander's zone of fire must never point at the cover the pusher walks. Both of you agreed it at the truck, and both wear orange.
scenarios.rule: Stander shoots only out of the cover, away from the pusher. Pushes are on foot only.
scenarios.p: Hunting with a partner: a simple push

scenarios.q: Your brother shoots a buck in MU (Management Unit) 2-19. His deer licence is back in the truck. He asks you to cancel yours on it.
ch: Do it: one tag is one tag
No: never use or lend a licence; he cancels his own
Do it and swap later
scenarios.why: Whoever kills big game cancels their own species licence, immediately and before handling it. Using another person's licence, or lending yours, is unlawful. Carry every licence on you.
scenarios.rule: Cancel your own species licence before you handle the animal. Never use or lend a licence.

scenarios.q: Your buck is down and dead in MU (Management Unit) 2-18. Dusk is coming. What do you do first?
ch: Drag it to the road before dark
Cancel your deer licence, then touch the deer
Field dress it, then tag it at the truck
scenarios.why: Kill, cancel, touch. Notch the licence immediately after the kill and before you handle the animal, the way the licence's own instructions say.
scenarios.rule: Cancel the species licence immediately after the kill and before handling the animal.

scenarios.q: Driving the Sts'ailes (West) FSR (Forest Service Road). A legal buck stands 60 m (66 yd) off the road. Your brother says shoot from the window.
ch: Shoot from the window
Don't: no hunting from a vehicle, and no loaded firearm in it
Shoot from the tailgate
scenarios.why: Hunting from a motor vehicle is unlawful, and so is a loaded firearm in or on one. Park, get out, walk away from the truck, then load where you may lawfully shoot.
scenarios.rule: No hunting from a motor vehicle (item 22). No loaded firearm in or on a vehicle (item 28).

scenarios.q: Back at the truck with a legal 2-19 buck, tagged. Your brother asks if you must book a compulsory inspection before you go home.
ch: Yes: every Region 2 deer is inspected
No: Region 2 inspection is for mountain goat and cougar, not deer
Yes: bring the head to an office
scenarios.why: Compulsory inspection in Region 2 is for mountain goat and cougar. Deer are not on the compulsory inspection or reporting lists. Keep the notched licence with the meat.
scenarios.rule: Region 2 compulsory inspection: mountain goat and cougar, not deer.

scenarios.q: Sunrise is in 40 minutes. A buck steps out, and a flock of ducks lands on the pond beside it. Both seasons are open.
ch: Both are legal now
Only the buck is legal now
Neither is legal yet
scenarios.why: Deer hours start 1 hour before sunrise. Duck hours start 30 minutes before sunrise, 10 minutes from now.
scenarios.rule: Big game: from 1 hour before sunrise. Migratory birds: from 30 minutes before sunrise.

scenarios.q: Walking in before legal light with your headlamp on, the beam catches a deer's eyes at 40 m (44 yd).
ch: Shoot: the light shows it clearly
Don't shoot: no hunting with a light, and it is before hours
Shoot only if you see antlers in the beam
scenarios.why: Hunting by the use of, or with the aid of, a light is unlawful. A headlamp to walk in is fine. Using it to hunt is not.
scenarios.rule: No hunting with a light or illuminating device. A headlamp to walk in before light is not hunting with a light (90%, the app's reading).
scenarios.lh: It is unlawful: items 35 to 38 (2 of 2)

scenarios.q: You hit a buck late in the day. You trail it and find it bedded, alive, 20 minutes after legal hours ended.
ch: Finish it: a wounded animal is an exception
Don't shoot: back out and return at first light
Shoot with your headlamp on it
scenarios.why: You cannot shoot a wounded animal after legal hours. No exception. Following a trail with a rifle is hunting. Back out, mark it, come back at first light. Call RAPP (Report All Poachers and Polluters) at 1 877 952 7277 for advice.
scenarios.rule: No shooting a wounded animal after legal hours, and no hunting with a light.
scenarios.p: page 11, item 38; page 3, definition of hunt
scenarios.lh: The law on hours and lights

scenarios.q: Your cancelled deer licence from last week is in a drawer at home. Today you hunt with your unused deer licence only.
ch: Fine: the cancelled one is used up
Go get it: carry every species licence for the year, used and unused
Fine if you have a photo of it
scenarios.why: Carry photo ID, your FWID (Fish and Wildlife ID) number and all your species licences for the licence year, cancelled and not.
scenarios.rule: Carry all your species licences for the year, used and unused, while hunting.

scenarios.q: Gutting your buck. Your brother says cut off the tail and testicles: the antlers prove it is a buck.
ch: Cut them off: antlers are enough
Keep the unskinned tail and a testicle or part of the penis attached
Keep only the head
scenarios.why: Antlers are not on the deer list. Evidence of sex stays naturally attached until the meat is home and butchered, at a meat cutter or cold storage, or inspected.
scenarios.rule: Buck: the unskinned tail and a testicle or part of the penis stay naturally attached.

scenarios.q: You stay at camp. A friend offers to drive your tagged deer home tonight.
ch: Fine, nothing needed
He needs a Record of Receipt from you
He needs his own deer licence
scenarios.why: Anyone moving wildlife killed by another person needs a Record of Receipt: date, place, your name and address, your FWID (Fish and Wildlife ID), the species licence number, species and sex.
scenarios.rule: Someone else carries your animal without you: Record of Receipt.

scenarios.q: You walk up to your deer and see it has no antlers. It is a doe, in a bucks only season. You have phone signal.
ch: Leave it and walk away
Cancel your licence, write in ink that you intend to self report, call RAPP
Tag it with your brother's licence
scenarios.why: Cancel the species licence at once and mark in ink that you intend to self report. Then call RAPP (Report All Poachers and Polluters), 1 877 952 7277, and follow the officer's direction.
scenarios.rule: Accidental illegal kill: cancel, write intent to self report, call RAPP.

scenarios.q: A buck stands on the gravel shoulder of a 2 lane paved public road the province maintains. You are parked and out of the truck.
ch: Shoot: you are out of the vehicle
Don't shoot: no hunting or shooting on the road allowance
Shoot if no car is coming
scenarios.why: On a numbered highway or a 2 lane public road the province maintains, you may not hunt within the road allowance, shoot within it or shoot across it. Under 3 lanes it runs 15 m (16 yd) each side of the middle.
scenarios.rule: No shooting across, shooting within, or hunting within the road allowance.

scenarios.q: You move the truck 300 m to the next pullout. Your brother keeps a round in the chamber to save time.
ch: Fine for a short drive
No: chamber and magazine empty in any vehicle
Fine if the safety is on
scenarios.why: No loaded firearm in or on a vehicle. Unloaded means no cartridge in the chamber and none in an attached or inserted magazine.
scenarios.rule: No loaded firearm in or on a vehicle. Chamber and attached magazine empty.

scenarios.q: You sit on the parked ATV (all terrain vehicle), engine off. A legal buck stands broadside at 70 m (77 yd).
ch: Shoot: the engine is off
Don't: an ATV is a motor vehicle, moving or parked
Shoot from the seat with a rest
scenarios.why: An ATV is a motor vehicle. No hunting from a motor vehicle, moving or parked. Get off and away from it first, then load.
scenarios.rule: No hunting from a motor vehicle. An ATV counts as one.

scenarios.q: Deer cross the road ahead. Your brother wants to drive the truck around the block to push them toward you.
ch: Good plan, deer move from trucks
No: herding wildlife with a vehicle is unlawful; pushes are on foot
Fine on a Forest Service Road
scenarios.why: It is unlawful to use a power boat, aircraft, motor vehicle or other mechanical device to herd or harass wildlife.
scenarios.rule: No herding or harassing wildlife with a vehicle, boat or aircraft.

scenarios.q: A hay field with no fence and no sign. A buck stands in the middle. You have not asked anyone.
ch: Shoot: no fence, no sign, so it is open
Don't shoot: cultivated land needs the owner's consent, posted or not
Shoot from the field edge
scenarios.why: Cultivated land needs the owner's, lessee's or occupant's consent even when it is not fenced or posted.
scenarios.rule: No hunting on cultivated land without consent.

scenarios.q: A farmer gave you permission last season. This November you go back without asking. A buck is on the back field.
ch: Shoot: you already have permission
Don't shoot: ask again, permission once does not cover later visits
Shoot and tell them after
scenarios.why: Unless explicitly stated, permission granted once does not entitle you to come back. One yes, one season. Get it in writing.
scenarios.rule: Permission granted once does not cover later occasions unless the owner says so.

scenarios.q: Region 2. A buck stands 70 m (77 yd) outside the edge of a regional district park.
ch: Shoot: you are outside the park
Don't shoot: no hunting or shooting within 100 m of a regional district park
Shoot if the bullet goes away from the park
scenarios.why: In Regions 1 and 2 you may not hunt or shoot within 100 m (109 yd) of any regional district park.
scenarios.rule: Regions 1 and 2: no hunting or shooting within 100 m of a regional district park.

scenarios.q: At a Forest recreation site, a buck stands 60 m (66 yd) from a picnic table and campsites.
ch: Shoot: nobody is camping today
Don't shoot: no firing into the developed part, 100 m from any structure or campsite
Shoot with a shotgun slug
scenarios.why: No shooting a firearm, bow or crossbow on or into the developed part of a recreation site. It reaches 100 m (109 yd) from any structure, day use area, campsite or staging area.
scenarios.rule: Recreation sites: no shooting on or into the developed portion, 100 m around it.

scenarios.q: Walking side by side in open timber. A buck runs left, out of your 45 degree slice, toward the ground in front of your brother.
ch: Keep swinging and shoot
Stop: let it go, it is out of your zone
Shout and shoot when it stops
scenarios.why: A zone of fire is the only slice of ground where you may shoot. Never swing the muzzle outside it, even tracking a running deer.
scenarios.rule: Shoot only inside your own zone, about 45 degrees ahead. Never swing past it.

scenarios.q: In thick timber you lose sight of your brother. A buck steps out ahead of you.
ch: Shoot: it is straight ahead of you
No shot: muzzle up or down, call out, fix the line first
Shoot if you heard him to your left
scenarios.why: Lose sight of each other: muzzles up or down, no shooting, call out. Close the gap so you keep sight.
scenarios.rule: Walk in a line, always in sight. Lose sight: no shooting until you have it back.
scenarios.lh: Two hunters walking side by side

scenarios.q: You reach a barbed wire fence on Crown land with a loaded rifle, safety on. Deer sign on the far side.
ch: Climb over carefully with the safety on
Unload, PROVE it safe, pass it through, cross away from the muzzle
Hand it over loaded to your brother
scenarios.why: Never climb a fence, log or bank with a loaded firearm. Alone: unload, lay it under or through, muzzle away, cross well away from the muzzle.
scenarios.rule: Unload before every fence, log or ditch.

scenarios.q: A buck stands where both of you could take it. You made no plan for who shoots.
ch: Both shoot at once to be sure
One shoots only, as you agree; next time agree at the truck
Whoever is faster shoots
scenarios.why: Only one of you shoots at a deer unless you agreed a backup plan first. Two shooters and no plan means a tag argument and a safety risk.
scenarios.rule: Agree who shoots before the hunt. Only the one who killed it tags it (99% for the tag).
scenarios.lh: Two armed hunters: you and your brother (1 of 2)

scenarios.q: Your brother's buck is down 60 m away. How do you both walk up to it?
ch: You run ahead with your rifle loaded
Both unload, walk up together, the shooter leads
The shooter waits while you go alone
scenarios.why: After a shot, both unload, then walk up together. The shooter leads, from behind and above the animal.
scenarios.rule: Both unload, walk up together, shooter first.
scenarios.p: Hunting with a partner: after the shot

scenarios.q: A buck stands on the ridge top, broadside, with only sky behind it.
ch: Shoot: broadside is the best angle
Don't shoot: no backstop, sky is never one
Shoot high to be safe
scenarios.why: A skylined animal has no backstop. A missed or passing bullet flies on for kilometres. Wait for it to step off the skyline.
scenarios.rule: Do not shoot at a skylined animal.

scenarios.q: A legal buck stands broadside. A doe stands right behind it, in line with your shot.
ch: Shoot: aim at the buck
Wait: the bullet exits, and the doe is your bullet too
Shoot both
scenarios.why: A rifle bullet usually passes through. Anything behind the animal is in the line of fire. Wait for a clear lane.
scenarios.rule: Another animal behind it: no shot.
scenarios.p: Shot placement: when not to shoot

scenarios.q: A buck stands broadside at 100 m (109 yd). Far behind it, in line, you glimpse a patch of orange: another hunter's vest.
ch: Shoot: the hunter is far away
Don't shoot: there is a person beyond
Shoot if the buck is on earth
scenarios.why: A safe backstop means earth behind the animal and no people, road, livestock or building beyond. A person beyond is a no.
scenarios.rule: Backstop: earth behind, nothing and nobody beyond.
scenarios.p: Is it legal to shoot? step 8; safety course rule
scenarios.lh: Steps 7 to 9: land, backstop, shot (1 of 2)

scenarios.q: Brown hair and movement in the salal at 50 m (55 yd). You think you saw an antler.
ch: Shoot: it is probably the buck
Don't shoot: not 100% sure what it is means no
Shoot low into the brush
scenarios.why: You must be 100% sure of species, sex and antlers before the shot. Brush can also deflect a bullet. Wait for a clear look.
scenarios.rule: Step 4: 100% sure what it is? Not sure means no.
scenarios.p: Is it legal to shoot? step 4

scenarios.q: A legal buck at 350 m (383 yd). You tested your rifle to 200 m (219 yd).
ch: Shoot: the scope reaches it
Don't shoot: beyond your tested range; close the distance or let it go
Aim high and shoot
scenarios.why: Your range test number is the law for you. Outside it, misses and wounded animals go up fast.
scenarios.rule: Clean shot inside your tested range only.
scenarios.p: Shot placement: when not to shoot

scenarios.q: A legal buck stands broadside at 80 m (87 yd), near front leg stepped forward. Steady rest, all 9 steps yes.
ch: Shoot: up the back of the front leg, one third up the chest
Shoot the neck to save meat
Don't shoot: wait for it to face you
scenarios.why: Broadside is the best angle. Up the back of the front leg, one third up the chest: both lungs and the top of the heart. The near leg forward opens the chest.
scenarios.rule: Aim for both lungs, just behind the shoulder, one third up the chest.

scenarios.q: A legal buck quarters away from you: you see its side and its rump, head turned away. 70 m (77 yd), steady rest.
ch: Shoot: aim so the bullet exits the far shoulder
Shoot the middle of the body
Never shoot a quartering animal
scenarios.why: Quartering away is the second best angle. Aim farther back on the near side so the bullet crosses both lungs and exits the far front shoulder.
scenarios.rule: Quartering away: good shot, aim toward the far shoulder.

scenarios.q: A buck quarters toward you: chest and near shoulder facing you, head toward you. Your first season.
ch: Shoot into the near shoulder
Wait for it to turn broadside
Shoot the head
scenarios.why: Quartering to puts heavy shoulder bone in the way and can deflect a light bullet. Beginners wait for the turn.
scenarios.rule: Quartering to: experienced hunters only. Wait.

scenarios.q: A buck faces straight at you at 60 m (66 yd), staring.
ch: Shoot the centre of the chest
Don't shoot: wait for it to turn
Shoot between the eyes
scenarios.why: Facing straight on: a small target between the shoulders, lots of bone, rarely a clean kill. Head shots are small, moving targets.
scenarios.rule: Facing straight on: rarely a clean kill. Head and neck shots: not for you.

scenarios.q: A buck walks straight away from you, white rump toward you, 50 m (55 yd).
ch: Shoot the base of the tail
Never: no vitals in reach; wait or let it go
Shoot when it looks back
scenarios.why: Walking straight away, no vitals are in reach. Guts and hams are in the way. Nobody takes that shot.
scenarios.rule: Rear end shots: never.

scenarios.q: A buck you jumped runs hard across a clearing at 80 m (87 yd).
ch: Lead it and shoot
Don't shoot: wait for it to stop; a soft whistle may stop it
Shoot where it will land
scenarios.why: It is hard to hit a vital on a moving animal. Wait for it to stop. A soft whistle or grunt often stops a deer (Tip).
scenarios.rule: Running animal: no shot. Wait for it to stop.

scenarios.q: A young buck lies bedded at 70 m (77 yd), only its head, ears and back showing.
ch: Shoot the visible back
Wait for it to stand
Shoot the head
scenarios.why: Lying down or sitting, the vitals are hidden or twisted. Wait for it to stand and turn.
scenarios.rule: Lying down or sitting: no shot, wait for it to stand.
scenarios.p: Outdoor Canada's bear rule, applied to deer

scenarios.q: Black bear season is open and you hold a bear licence. A lone adult black bear stands broadside, near leg forward, 60 m (66 yd).
ch: Aim halfway up the body, tight behind the shoulder
Aim one third up like a deer, far back
Aim at the head
scenarios.why: On a bear the heart sits low and the lungs reach back. Hair and fat make it look bigger. Halfway up, tight behind the shoulder, through both lungs. No head or shoulder shots.
scenarios.rule: Black bear: halfway up the body, tight behind the shoulder, near leg forward.

scenarios.q: Your buck mule kicked and ran hard. At the hit site: bright pink, bubbly blood.
ch: Follow right away
Mark the spot and wait about 30 minutes
Wait 12 hours
scenarios.why: Pink, frothy blood often means a lung hit. Wait about 30 minutes, then follow. Flag where it stood and where you last saw it.
scenarios.rule: Heart or lungs: wait about 30 minutes.
scenarios.lh: After the hit, by zone (1 of 2)

scenarios.q: The buck hunched up and walked off slowly. At the hit site: thin, greenish brown blood that smells of stomach.
ch: Follow now before it gets far
Back out quietly and wait hours
Wait 10 minutes, then push it
scenarios.why: A gut hit beds nearby if not pushed. Pushed, it runs and is often lost. Sources say wait 4 to 12 hours. The wait is your call; hours, not minutes.
scenarios.rule: Paunch hit: back out, wait hours (4 to 12, sources differ).

scenarios.q: The blood trail leads under a fence with a No Trespassing sign. The deer is probably just past it.
ch: Cross: tracking wounded game is an exception
Stop: ask the owner first; no answer, call a conservation officer
Cross without your rifle
scenarios.why: The Trespass Act has no exception for tracking wounded game. Get the owner's permission first, in writing if you can.
scenarios.rule: Fenced or posted land: no tracking exception. Ask the owner.

scenarios.q: You lose the blood trail after 10 minutes. Rain is starting. Your brother says call it a day.
ch: Go home: you tried
Back to the last blood, circle at 20 m then 40 m, then lanes with your brother
Wait in the truck until tomorrow
scenarios.why: You must make all reasonable effort to find, finish and retrieve a wounded animal. Walking away after 10 minutes is not reasonable effort. Rain erases blood fast, so go now.
scenarios.rule: All reasonable effort to locate, dispatch and retrieve wounded game, and count it in your bag.
scenarios.lh: You must try to recover it

scenarios.q: Your buck lies still 40 m (44 yd) ahead after the wait. How do you come in?
ch: From the legs side, to grab the antlers
From behind its back, rifle ready; touch the eye with a stick
Run in fast before it gets up
scenarios.why: A live deer can kick or jump up. Come from behind the back, rifle ready, watch the chest. Touch the eye with a stick: no blink means dead.
scenarios.rule: Approach from the spine side, rifle ready, eye touch test.
scenarios.p: After the shot: approach and notch

scenarios.q: An unwounded buck swims across the lake in front of you, in season.
ch: Shoot: it can't escape
Don't shoot: big game swimming is off limits unless already wounded
Shoot when it reaches shallow water
scenarios.why: It is unlawful to hunt, wound or kill big game while it is swimming, unless it has been previously wounded.
scenarios.rule: No shooting big game while it swims, unless it is already wounded.
scenarios.lh: It is unlawful: items 25 to 29 (1 of 2)

scenarios.q: You reach your planned trailhead before light. Another truck is already parked at the pullout.
ch: Hunt it anyway, it is public land
Drive on to another spot
Park beside it and walk faster
scenarios.why: A truck at a pullout means someone is on that ridge. Find your own ridge. Pressure and crossed paths make it unsafe and unfair.
scenarios.rule: Someone got there first: hunt a different spot.

scenarios.q: Stalking a buck, you see another hunter already crawling toward it from the side.
ch: Shoot first before they do
Back out quietly
Shout to warn the deer
scenarios.why: Walking in on another hunter's stalk is the worst thing short of a bad shot. It is also unlawful to interfere with a person lawfully hunting.
scenarios.rule: Do not interfere with or obstruct a person lawfully hunting.

scenarios.q: On a trail, you meet two hunters coming the other way, rifles on their shoulders.
ch: Keep your rifle loaded and walk past
Unload, muzzle down, say where you are headed and ask where they are
Step off the trail and hide
scenarios.why: Meet on a trail: unload, muzzle down, say where you are headed and ask where they will be. Now neither of you shoots toward the other.
scenarios.rule: Meeting other hunters: unload, muzzle down, share your routes.

scenarios.q: Field dressing your buck at dusk in MU (Management Unit) 2-19. A black bear stands 40 m (44 yd) away, watching, not reacting.
ch: Shoot it before it takes your deer
Run to the truck
Talk calmly, back away slowly, spray in hand
scenarios.why: Aware but calm: speak softly and back away slowly. Never run. A bear is not a target unless it is legal game in season under your licence or a real threat to life.
scenarios.rule: Never run from a bear. Calm voice, back away, spray ready.

scenarios.q: A bear pops its jaws, woofs and stomps. It bluff charges and stops short at 15 m (16 yd).
ch: Run downhill
Calm voice, back away slowly, keep it in sight, spray ready
Charge it back
scenarios.why: Jaw popping, woofing, stomping and bluff charges are warnings from a stressed, defensive bear. Most bluff charges stop short. Give it room. Never run.
scenarios.rule: Agitated bear: calm voice, back away, no direct eye contact, spray ready.

scenarios.q: A bear comes straight at you and is now about 8 m (9 yd) away. Spray on your hip, rifle on your back.
ch: Spray now, aimed low in front of its head
Wait until it touches you
Turn and run
scenarios.why: Use spray when the bear is within about 5 to 10 m. At 6 to 9 m, short bursts aimed low in front of the head. Studies found spray stopped bears more often than guns.
scenarios.rule: Spray on the hip, used within about 5 to 10 m.

scenarios.q: You come back for the hung meat at first light. From a distance you glass it: the quarters are moved and partly buried.
ch: Walk in fast and grab what is left
Leave the area and report it
Scare the bear off with a shot
scenarios.why: A moved or buried carcass means a bear has claimed it. Do not approach. Leave and report. Do not try to scare a bear off a carcass.
scenarios.rule: Carcass moved or buried, or a bear on it: do not approach, leave and report.

scenarios.q: Black bear season is open and you hold a bear licence. A sow walks out with two cubs behind her.
ch: Shoot the sow, the cubs are big enough
Don't shoot: a cub, and any bear with it, is off limits
Shoot one cub
scenarios.why: It is unlawful to hunt a black bear under 2 years old, or any bear in its company. The sow with cubs is protected.
scenarios.rule: No hunting a black bear under 2, or a bear with it.

scenarios.q: You hold a black bear licence. A brown bear with a high shoulder hump, dished face and small round ears walks across the slide.
ch: Shoot: brown black bears are legal
Don't shoot: the hump and face say grizzly, and there is no open season
Shoot if it is alone
scenarios.why: Colour does not tell you the species. Hump, face and ears do. There is no open season for grizzly bears in BC.
scenarios.rule: No open season for grizzly bears in BC.
scenarios.lh: Why grizzly hunting is closed in BC

scenarios.q: You surprised a bear at close range. It knocks you down in a fast, noisy, defensive attack.
ch: Lie still on your stomach, pack on, hands over your neck
Fight back at its face
Get up and run
scenarios.why: Defensive attack: once it makes contact, lie still on your stomach, hands clasped over the back of your neck, feet apart. Stay still until it leaves. A predatory attack that keeps going: fight.
scenarios.rule: Defensive contact: lie still. Predatory: fight back.

scenarios.q: You and your brother start field dressing a buck in bear country above Harrison. How do you set up?
ch: Both work quietly, rifles leaned on a tree 20 m away
One works and talks, one watches, rifle and spray in reach
Drag the deer back to camp first
scenarios.why: Make noise while dressing: scent draws bears. One of you watches. Move the meat at least 200 m from the gut pile and get it out fast. Dragging it to camp lays a scent trail to you.
scenarios.rule: Kill site: noise, a lookout, meat 200 m from the gut pile, out fast.
